mcat_description.short: A Naturally Ventilated Polyhouse (NVPH) is a prefabricated protected cultivation structure with a hot-dip galvanised (GI) steel pipe frame covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film, relying on passive roof and side vents for temperature and airflow regulation without mechanical cooling systems.
mcat_description.long: Naturally Ventilated Polyhouses (NVPHs) are agricultural greenhouse structures designed for protected cultivation of high-value vegetables, flowers, and nursery crops in Indian agro-climatic conditions. The structure consists of a hot-dip galvanised GI pipe framework (conforming to IS 1161 and IS 4759:2019), covered with 200-micron UV-stabilised polyethylene film, with roof vents and side vents enabling passive airflow via the stack effect — warm air exits through the ridge and cool air enters through side openings. NVPHs are the most widely adopted protected cultivation structure in India, eligible for up to 50% government subsidy under NHM/NHB/MIDH schemes, with standard sizes ranging from 500 sq. mt to 4,000 sq. mt as per NHM model specifications. They are sold as complete turnkey structures or as prefabricated component kits, customised to wind load, crop type, and regional climate requirements.

market_context: In the Indian market, 'Naturally Ventilated Polyhouse' (NVPH) and 'Naturally Ventilated Poly House' are used interchangeably with 'polyhouse' as the dominant trade term; 'greenhouse' is the more formal or export-facing term for the same structure. The NHM designation 'Open Vent Polyhouse (OVPH)' is used in government subsidy documentation. NHB and NHM/MIDH technical standards define the canonical structural specifications: GI pipe frame (IS 1161, IS 4759:2019), 200-micron UV-stabilised PE film, gutter height 4.0–4.5 m, ridge height 6.0–6.5 m, nut-bolt assembly (no site welding). Government subsidy eligibility under NHM/NHB/MIDH (up to 50% for general farmers, up to 60–65% with state top-ups) is a primary purchase driver — buyers frequently search for 'NHB subsidy polyhouse' and 'NHM approved polyhouse'. Standard project sizes range from 500 sq. mt to 4,000 sq. mt under NHM norms. Key buyer segments are progressive farmers, commercial horticulture entrepreneurs, and state-empanelled contractors. The NVPH is the most cost-effective protected cultivation structure in India, positioned between the cheaper shade net house and the more expensive fan-and-pad climate-controlled polyhouse. Major manufacturing hubs include Gujarat (Surat), Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh/Telangana. Israeli greenhouse technology influence is noted in premium segment designs (Agriplast). Crops most commonly grown: coloured capsicum, tomato, cucumber (vegetables); rose, gerbera, carnation (floriculture).
